Dana: quick RFC follow-up: propose a small "profiling slab" between SMOKE and full VALIDATION. idea is to catch perf tail/kv regressions cheaply before expensive evals.
Harper: outline the assertions?
Dana: profiling slab asserts deterministic load, kv-cache shape, kernel-selection parity, and tail latency profile on a microbench (p99, p999) using a handful of replayed traces (~200 requests). also capture memory-growth and ephemeral alloc spikes.
Lin: how is this different from COMPAT? COMPAT already does deterministic checks.
Dana: COMPAT is binary/determinism heavy; profiling slab focuses on runtime tail behavior and microbenching under realistic batching/sequence mixes. cheaper than full validation but more performance-focused than COMPAT.
Miguel: cost? running p999 benches can be noisy and long.
Dana: keep it bounded: run 3 short microbench shards (30-90s each) sampling short/med/long seq buckets. use warmup + steady-state windows to compute p99/p999. If p999 delta > threshold vs baseline, fail fast and trigger full VALIDATION.
Harper: thresholds and ownership?
Lin: suggest thresholds: p99_delta <= 10% and p999_delta <= 25% by default. eng-ml owns infra and microbench harness; eng-sre reviews quota impact. product-ops gets the alert stream.
Miguel: Console UX: add profiling_signal with small report link. Rollout policy can require profiling_pass for strict tenants.
Dana: intake fingerprint must include exports: kv_layout_hash + export_tool + expected_kv_strides so profiling can do deterministic mapping. small intake example: "kv_layout_hash: sha256:11ab", "export_tool: torchscript-2x".
Harper: what about flaky results on noisy hosts? we should run benches on dedicated ci-small pool to reduce variance.
Dana: agreed — use a controlled CI pool and seed randomness. also persist recent baseline runs to compute stable deltas (median of 3 runs).
Miguel: action items: 1) Dana+Lin: draft profiling asserts + thresholds, 2) Harper: estimate infra delta and recommend ci-pool size, 3) Lin: Console flag + small report format, 4) eng-sre: reserve quota gating.
onboard-bot: created ticket ONB-11422 "profiling-slab: microbench spec and baseline policy" (assignee: Dana).
Harper: +1. if we can catch tail regressions early this will save lots of full-validations.
Dana: thanks all, i'll put up a short PRD and link ONB-11422. closing thread.
